steps_json: Stop the task and secure the crew member and loose objects nearby.
Ask what happened, where it hurts and whether they blacked out.
Check that they know their name, the date and where they are.
Look for swelling, a bent shape or pain when moving the limb.
Hold a cold pack wrapped in cloth on the area for 15 minutes.
Keep a painful limb still with the splint from the drawer.
Repeat the name, date and place check every 15 minutes for 2 hours.
escalation_en: Call the crew physician now if they blacked out, vomit, are confused, have a severe headache, cannot move the limb or the limb looks bent.
source_en: World Health Organization. Basic Emergency Care: approach to the acutely ill and injured (2018).

steps_json: Put on gloves from the drawer before touching the wound.
Press a clean gauze pad firmly on the cut for 10 minutes without lifting it.
If blood soaks through, add more gauze on top and keep pressing.
Once bleeding stops, rinse the cut with clean water to remove debris.
Close small cuts with adhesive strips and cover with a dry dressing.
Capture the floating droplets with absorbent wipes and bag them.
Check the dressing and the skin around it twice a day for redness or warmth.
escalation_en: Call the crew physician now if bleeding does not stop after 10 minutes of firm pressure, the cut is deep or gaping, or there is numbness beyond the wound.
source_en: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines (2020).

title_en: Taking Medicine Safely and Side Effects
steps_json: Read the label and check the name, dose and expiry date before taking it.
Confirm with the crew physician before starting any new medicine.
Log the medicine, dose and time in the health log right away.
Do not take two medicines with the same active ingredient at once.
Avoid sleep aids within 8 hours of a piloting or repair shift.
Watch for rash, itching, dizziness, stomach upset or unusual sleepiness.
If a side effect appears, stop the medicine and log what you feel.
escalation_en: Call the crew physician now if there is swelling of the face or throat, trouble breathing, a spreading rash or fainting after taking a medicine.
source_en: World Health Organization. Model List of Essential Medicines, 23rd list (2023).
